# Repository Guidelines

## Agent bootstrap

Read `.ai/rules/common.md`, `.ai/service.yaml`, `docs/README.md`, and affected HTTP, event, database, lifecycle, or integration contracts before changing files. Production code, migrations, tests, and repository-owned docs are authoritative.

## Architecture invariants

- This service owns student onboarding profiles, ordinary Course attempts/reviews, selected positions, progression, raw learning evidence, and mastery projections. V2 practice-task catalog and runtime state belong to `ms-go-practice-task-orchestrator`; legacy `student_practice_task*` rows are read-only compatibility history by default. Self-assessed experience is an initial hypothesis, never diagnosed mastery.
- Keep domain/use-case logic independent from chi, pgx, NATS, and HTTP clients. Adapters implement repository and service boundaries; `cmd/ms-student-service/main.go` is the composition root.
- Live validation is UX feedback owned by Sandbox. Student owns official ordinary Course-attempt status; Practice owns v2 practice submission/result status.
- Attempt status values, evaluation/submission modes, structured-assessment shapes, progression rules, practice-task bindings, database schema, NATS subjects, and downstream payloads are contracts.
- Do not create or mutate legacy student practice-task runtime unless the explicit emergency compatibility flag is enabled. The default writer routes return `410 Gone` and name Practice as owner.
- Prefer the exact starter workspace and runtime profile stored in the pinned revision. Local milestone-kind builders and runtime switches are legacy fallback only when those revision fields are absent; malformed authored values must fail closed.
- Student runtime must never receive or infer private test-suite/reference-solution/negative-fixture/verifier artifacts from the catalog runtime context.
- Final-review submission must re-run every selected milestone contract in `final` mode against the current sandbox snapshot before AI or mentor review. Private suite references prove the authoring gates and remain opaque; this service does not execute repository scripts by path.
- Final-review policy version 1 always requires a mentor. AI review is optional infrastructure and advisory only: sanitize workspace input, validate structured output, apply the configured unavailable fallback, and never turn AI failure into deterministic student failure or let AI complete the project.
- AI-review contracts and mentor rubrics must be loaded only from the pinned revision's internal evaluation context. Student-facing review history must not expose either private contract.
- A portfolio publication may be created only from the immutable artifact referenced by a passed mentor review for a completed student practice task. Never publish the live sandbox, a preview URL, storage IDs, private evaluation data, AI prompts, or mentor rubrics.
- Portfolio visibility is `private`, `unlisted`, or `public`. Both `unlisted` and `public` may be read by the opaque share slug; only `public` appears in the student's public listing. Returning to `private` must revoke link access immediately.
- Public code is a separately sanitized, immutable, text-only snapshot. Reject possible inline secrets, automatically omit sensitive/system/dependency/binary files, expose the omission paths only to the owner, and serve public endpoints with revocation-safe cache policy.
- `ms-go-filestorage` currently exposes file download without a trustworthy authorization boundary. Publication snapshots must therefore be encrypted before upload and decrypted only in this service after the database visibility check. Never return the storage file ID or encryption key.
- Public portfolio APIs are read-only. They must not open a terminal, mutate files, create a sandbox session, run code, or expose a direct link to live sandbox/preview infrastructure.
- When a selected variant contains explicit lesson bindings, they are authoritative for practice-task roadmap and access. Only required lessons block a milestone; recommended/optional lessons remain visible and skippable. Use skill-tag matching only for legacy milestones without explicit bindings.
- Required alternative_group bindings are one-of. Lessons in one prerequisite_group are a same-stage set and do not block one another; required units in earlier route stages block later lessons.
- Student/admin HTTP identity currently trusts `X-User-ID` and `X-User-Role`; internal routes use a shared token. Do not describe these as JWT verification or end-to-end authentication.
- Most PostgreSQL writes, sandbox calls, runtime finalization, and legacy NATS publications are not one transaction. Preserve idempotency and explicitly test partial-failure behavior. `learning_action.closed` is the producer-side exception: answer closure, action closure, and outbox insert commit atomically. The consumed teacher-assistance path is a separate durable inbox transaction and must acknowledge only after commit.
- `LearningAction` is a distinct cycle linked to an answer, never an alias for `student_task_answer.id`. Start opens one cycle, `UNDER_REVIEW` keeps it open, terminal `FAILED`/`PASSED` closes it, and activity after `FAILED`/`REJECTED` opens a new cycle. Freeze ordered task learning targets when the cycle opens and never infer missing targets.
- Freeze the task evidence class when a learning action opens and its official outcome when it closes. Mastery policy `student-mastery-v1` runs only after exact Teacher assistance correlation, is cumulative/replay-safe, and remains wholly owned by this service. Never assume independent work after a timeout or backfill legacy action outcomes from mutable answer state.
- Accept v2 Practice evidence only through the strict internal versioned contract. Require exact versioned targets, UUID idempotency, immutable raw evidence, assistance-aware support context, the shared mastery reducer, and a separate reducer audit.
- Legacy CSS validation sends every CSS/SCSS/ACSS source to the existing NATS engine with an empty provider rubric; task criteria remain the preceding local code_structure checks. Missing stylesheets fail, indented Sass is unsupported, and malformed/protocol/unavailable or internal.compiler_error replies remain technical errors rather than learner failures. Semantic feedback permits only the provider's eight known rule codes, exact workspace path/position and a static safe message; unknown codes and arbitrary provider text never cross this boundary.

## Verification and delivery

- Use `.ai/commands.yaml`; run policy, tracked-file `gofmt`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./... -count=1`, and build verification.
- Lifecycle, scoring, progression, event, schema, or integration changes require focused regression tests and synchronized owned documentation.
- Do not start services, Docker/PostgreSQL/NATS, apply/roll back migrations, contact sibling services, or run E2E scenarios without approval. Migration rollback is destructive and incomplete.
